skill.name: request-refactor-plan
skill.description: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits through a user interview, repository review, testing discussion, and GitHub issue template.
skill.summary: Turn refactor ideas into scoped GitHub issues with tiny, safe commits.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only file. I found no semantic evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Large refactors can stall when scope, decisions, and tests are unclear. This skill guides an interview, verifies the codebase, and turns the plan into a GitHub issue.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user to clarify the refactor problem and possible solutions.
Explores the repository to verify assumptions before planning changes.
Defines scope, out-of-scope work, implementation decisions, and testing decisions.
Breaks refactors into tiny commits that keep the project working.
Creates a GitHub issue using a structured refactor plan template.
Avoids specific file paths and code snippets in the generated issue body.
limitations: It plans refactors but does not implement code changes by itself.
It needs repository access to verify assumptions and inspect test coverage.
GitHub issue creation requires available GitHub tooling and user authorization.
The plan quality depends on clear answers during the interview.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Risky Refactor
use_cases.description: Turn a broad architecture change into a reviewed plan with small commits and testing notes.

use_cases.title: Align a Team Before Work Starts
use_cases.description: Create a GitHub issue that records scope, decisions, testing plans, and unresolved notes.

use_cases.title: Learn Safe Refactoring Habits
use_cases.description: Use a guided interview to understand tradeoffs before changing unfamiliar code.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small code cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a refactor for this repository. I want to clean up the authentication flow without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Team RFC
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for team review before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me and create a refactor plan issue for replacing our legacy settings module with a clearer service boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Scope and Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for confirming risk before filing an issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a refactor for our billing workflow. Verify the current code, identify test gaps, and separate required work from out-of-scope ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a complex incremental migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue for migrating our data access layer. Break it into tiny commits and document decisions, testing, and rollout boundaries.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to simplify a legacy permissions module.
output_examples.output: A refactor issue with the problem, proposed solution, tiny commit plan, decisions, testing choices, and out-of-scope items.

output_examples.input: A team needs agreement before replacing a shared service boundary.
output_examples.output: A planning conversation followed by a GitHub issue that records tradeoffs, scope, and safe migration steps.

output_examples.input: A maintainer is unsure whether existing tests cover a refactor area.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan that identifies relevant test coverage, test gaps, and behavior-focused testing decisions.

best_practices: Provide a detailed problem statement and any solution ideas before the interview starts.
Let the assistant inspect the repository before accepting assumptions about the current design.
Review the final GitHub issue for scope, decisions, and test coverage before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to skip design review for high-risk architecture changes.
Do not ask it to implement the refactor before the plan is agreed.
Do not include volatile file paths or code snippets in the GitHub issue body.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates a refactor plan and GitHub issue so implementation can happen in reviewed steps.

faq.question: Why does it interview the user first?
faq.answer: The interview captures goals, constraints, alternatives, and decisions that repository inspection alone cannot reveal.

faq.question: Can it create a GitHub issue automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, if GitHub tooling is available and the user authorizes the action.

faq.question: What makes the commit plan useful?
faq.answer: It breaks the refactor into small steps that should keep the codebase working after each commit.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks existing coverage and records behavior-focused testing decisions in the plan.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
